observations:
Torah LM2/48 is a short pastoral letter (19 lines) of encouragement addressed to one beginning divine service. The spec for new packages requires '3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language in the source text that form an independent domain not covered by the existing packages.' This criterion is not met.

The source text contains exactly two bechina equations (both currently missing from the dataset — see additions file):

1. הִתְרַחֲקוּת ↔ הִתְקָרְבוּת — the appearance of distancing IS drawing-close (2 nodes, 1 bechina edge)
2. עַצְבוּת ↔ סִטְרָא אָחֳרָא — sadness IS the sitra achra (2 nodes, 1 bechina edge)

Each bechina equation is a pair of 2 nodes, which is below the threshold of 3+ needed to declare a 'new package' with an independent domain.

Once the two missing bechina edges are added to the dataset, the natural package structure would be:

  POTENTIAL PACKAGE A (neutral/paradox domain): הִתְרַחֲקוּת + הִתְקָרְבוּת
  Dominant node: הִתְקָרְבוּת (the true reality behind the appearance)
  This 2-node cluster is still below the 3-node threshold for a formal package proposal.

  POTENTIAL PACKAGE B (evil domain): עַצְבוּת + סִטְרָא אָחֳרָא
  Dominant node: עַצְבוּת (explicitly identified with the sitra achra)
  This 2-node cluster is still below the 3-node threshold.

Cluster candidates examined and rejected:

1. שִׂמְחָה + הִתְחַזְּקוּת + עַקְשָׁנוּת cluster: These three positive concepts — joy, self-strengthening, stubborn persistence — are all advocated in the teaching and share the same functional domain (the positive qualities needed for divine service). However, the Rebbe never connects any two of them with 'X הוּא בְּחִינַת Y' language. They appear as co-equal imperatives in an eitza chain (do these things → enter holiness), not as bechina-equivalent aspects of a single essence. Without explicit bechina language connecting them, no package can be formed.

2. גַּשְׁמִיּוּת + עַצְבוּת + יְרִידוֹת cluster: These three obstacles — materiality, sadness, and falls — are all described as the forces that block divine service. Only עַצְבוּת is explicitly identified with the sitra achra via bechina. The others are causal antagonists in the eitza structure. Without explicit bechina equations connecting them, this cluster cannot form a package.

3. גֶּשֶׁר צַר + הִתְרַחֲקוּת + שַׁעֲרֵי הַקְּדֻשָּׁה cluster: These are three spatial/structural metaphors in the teaching. The narrow bridge, the gates of holiness, and the appearance of distance are all used as images in the same narrative, but none is equated as a bechina of another via identity language. The bridge is a mashal (parable), not a bechina concept.

CONCLUSION: Torah LM2/48 is a practical letter with a predominantly eitza structure. Its teaching is: persist in service → distance is really closeness → sadness (= sitra achra) is the obstacle → joy and stubbornness are the tools → you will enter holiness. The conceptual flow is entirely causal. The two bechina equations it contains are brief, citation-backed identifications (not developed bechina clusters), and each yields only a 2-node pair — insufficient for package formation under the 3+ threshold.
